label: More on Bracket Algebra
notes: Open by framing the chapter's reversal of viewpoint: brackets, not coordinates, become the primary data of a configuration. Across printed pages 109 to 126 we build the bracket ring, meet the Grassmann-Plucker syzygies, and use straightening to decide equality of bracket expressions and to certify geometric theorems algebraically.

label: The Determinant Vector
notes: Define the bracket as a three-by-three determinant and assemble all of them into the determinant vector Gamma of P. Stress the two transformation laws: a projective map multiplies every bracket by one common determinant factor, while rescaling a column multiplies only brackets containing that letter. These laws drive everything later.

label: The Ring of Bracket Polynomials
notes: Introduce bracket variables as abstract symbols and the ring of polynomials in them. The point is that not every assignment of numbers to brackets comes from real points; the determinant expansion map identifies which polynomials vanish, and its kernel is the ideal we must understand.

label: Grassmann-Plucker Relations
notes: Present the Grassmann-Plucker relations as the defining syzygies of the bracket ring. Write the three-term and the longer expansion explicitly. Emphasize these quadratic relations are not optional identities: they are exactly the consistency conditions making arbitrary bracket numbers behave like genuine determinants of point coordinates.

label: Standard Tableaux Basis
notes: Explain that bracket monomials map to Young tableaux, and that monomials whose rows are sorted and whose columns weakly increase are called standard. The standard tableaux form a vector-space basis for the bracket ring, giving every bracket expression a unique canonical normal form once we can reach it.

label: The Straightening Algorithm
notes: Walk through straightening: any non-standard monomial has a violating column, and a Grassmann-Plucker relation rewrites it as a signed sum of lexicographically smaller monomials. Iterating terminates in the standard basis. This is the engine that decides equality of bracket expressions by reducing their difference to zero.

label: Straightening a Monomial
notes: Do a concrete straightening on the diagram. The non-standard product on the left has a column inversion; applying the relation replaces it with standard terms on the right. Point out the bookkeeping of signs and that the canonical result no longer depends on the order operations were applied.

label: Reconstruction from Brackets
notes: Show the converse direction echoed in the notebook: normalizing one nonzero bracket to one lets us rebuild a representative matrix, reading later columns straight from brackets. The first three columns become the standard basis, and Grassmann-Plucker relations force every remaining bracket, recovering the configuration up to projective equivalence.

label: Projective Invariants as Bracket Ratios
notes: Define a bracket monomial ratio as projectively invariant when numerator and denominator share total degree and per-point weight, so all column and determinant scalings cancel. Write the cross-ratio of four collinear points as a balanced quotient with an auxiliary off-line anchor, then connect to the notebook's scaling lab.

label: First Fundamental Theorem
notes: State the first fundamental theorem of invariant theory: every projective invariant of point configurations is a polynomial in the brackets. This is why geometry translates to bracket algebra at all, turning incidence statements into algebraic identities and giving straightening universal reach over projectively meaningful quantities.

label: Theorems as Bracket Identities
notes: Encode Pappos as a bracket polynomial that, on the hypothesis of collinear triples, must straighten to zero. The diagram shows the two lines, their six points, and the conclusion line. Proving the theorem becomes a finite, mechanical straightening computation rather than a coordinate chase.

label: Final Polynomials
notes: Close with final polynomials: a bracket certificate that a combinatorial configuration cannot be realized over the reals. A sign-definite bracket combination that the Grassmann-Plucker relations force to be simultaneously positive and zero is the non-realizability proof. Recap the arc from determinant vector to certificate.
